name: Abstract Security × Microsoft Sentinel
tagline: SIEM is a state of mind. Abstract is the world's first Composable SIEM — assemble collection, detection, retention and AI-SecOps by design, not by lock-in.
description: A reusable SE / evaluation profile describing the transparent, bidirectional Abstract<->Sentinel integration: how they connect, where they overlap or complement, and the augment/optimize/rebalance path.
positioning: Abstract is the world's first Composable SIEM (collection · detection · retention · AI-SecOps); Microsoft Sentinel is one composable component you keep, augment, or rebalance.

manifesto.title: The Composable SIEM Manifesto — SIEM is a State of Mind
manifesto.lede: “SIEM is a state of mind.” Not a box, not a single vendor — an organizational philosophy of adaptability, modularity, and choice. Abstract built the world's first **Composable SIEM**: collection, detection, retention, and AI-enabled security operations as independent, interoperable building blocks you assemble by design — with Microsoft Sentinel as one composable component you keep, augment, or rebalance.

tenets.tenet: Next-Gen SIEM is not a SIEM
tenets.detail: The true next generation breaks the monolith — it isn't a glorified log store with a new coat of paint.
Detect in the stream, before data becomes expensive, rigid, or locked in. Prioritize signal over noise, outcomes over ingestion volume.
Most collected security data is never used for detection. Store data intelligently — right data, right tier, right place — not everything in one indexed box.

tenets.tenet: AI is baked in, not bolted on
tenets.detail: Born in the AI era: AI-GEN is stream-first and composable by design. Without normalized, streaming, contextual data, AI is blind, shallow, and late.

tenets.tenet: AI-SOC is a capability, not a category
tenets.detail: Like SOAR before it, AI-SOC collapses into the fabric. AI augments SIEM across triage, investigation and response — it doesn't replace it.
Not fragmented, not complex — an architecture of choice. Pick components and vendors per outcome, evolve incrementally, no forced re-architecture.

buildingBlocks.what: The control plane where data is shaped, normalized and enriched before it becomes expensive or locked in — feeding many downstream systems, not one monolith.
buildingBlocks.withSentinel: Feeds Sentinel (and any SIEM) clean, enriched, cost-reduced data via the destination + insights connectors.

buildingBlocks.what: Portable detection logic — in-stream, historical, and federated — that runs where the data lives. Detection is no longer bound to storage.
buildingBlocks.withSentinel: Complements Sentinel analytics: shift-left convictions arrive as high-fidelity insights; Sentinel rules still run on what lands.

buildingBlocks.what: Tiered + federated storage: high-signal data near detection, everything else affordable and still query-ready (LakeVilla, replay, no rehydration).
buildingBlocks.withSentinel: Route full fidelity to LakeVilla, send only convictions + context to Sentinel's hot tier — the big cost lever.

buildingBlocks.what: AI embedded across triage, investigation, hunting and response — ASTRO enabling analysts, not replacing them, over pipeline-clean data + context.
buildingBlocks.withSentinel: ASTRO auto-triages and reasons; results flow back to Sentinel incidents via playbooks, Copilot and MCP.

valueProps.title: Cut SIEM cost at the source
valueProps.detail: Abstract aggregates, dedupes, filters and routes upstream — the SIEM bill is volume-driven, so cutting volume before ingest cuts the bill. Demo: ~34:1 aggregation and ~99.6% volume routed away from the SIEM.

valueProps.title: Shift-left detection
valueProps.detail: Six in-stream detections (verdict fusion, IOC blast-match, beaconing/C2, ATO↔C2 bridge, lateral/exfil, campaign clustering) fire in ~0.5s — before data lands — vs. SIEM ingest+schedule latency.

valueProps.title: 100% enrichment, upstream
valueProps.detail: A 5-step in-stream chain (identity/asset resolution, geo/ASN, TI/AIG IOC match, 29+ OSINT adapters, verdict fusion) enriches every event before it lands. The SIEM receives conclusions, not raw noise.

valueProps.title: ASTRO — the AI SOC engine
valueProps.detail: ASTRO is Abstract's AI security engineer, embedded natively in the platform — not a generic chatbot. It runs agentic triage, investigation and detection-tuning over pipeline-clean, correlated, enriched data and full case context: a grounded verdict + recommended actions before an analyst opens the case (e.g. Verdict, IP Threat Intelligence) — and considerably more.

valueProps.title: Compliance handled in-stream
valueProps.detail: Abstract states it detects and redacts PII in-stream (GDPR/HIPAA/PCI) before data lands anywhere, and normalizes to OCSF, ECS or Splunk CIM — so the same clean data fits any destination and sensitive fields never hit the SIEM.

valueProps.title: Destination- & source-agnostic — less lock-in
valueProps.detail: Normalize once to OCSF/ACS (473 fields); route the same events, detections and findings to Sentinel, Splunk, any SIEM, Event Hub, or LakeVilla. Pick destinations per-cost, not per-capability.

valueProps.title: Retroactive hunts without rehydration
valueProps.detail: Full-fidelity telemetry lives in LakeVilla, always query-ready; replay a new IOC through live detections across 90+ days to find historical victims — no SIEM archive rehydration cost.

valueProps.title: Microsoft is validating the model
valueProps.detail: Microsoft's own moves — Auxiliary/Basic logs tiers, the Sentinel data lake, and Defender XDR correlation — validate cheap tiered storage and pre-SIEM curation. Abstract does it upstream and vendor-agnostic, so the savings and the detections travel with you across SIEMs, not just within one.

capabilityGap.sentinel: Cloud-native SIEM/SOAR — detect, investigate, respond over *ingested* data.
capabilityGap.abstract: Security data pipeline — normalize, enrich, correlate, detect and route *before* ingest (shift-left).
capabilityGap.whyItMatters: They occupy different layers: a pipeline in front of a SIEM is complementary, not a like-for-like swap.

capabilityGap.sentinel: Priced per GB ingested + retention; cost scales with raw volume (unified Analytics ~$4.30/GB PAYG, East US; commitment tiers save up to 52%).
capabilityGap.abstract: Reduce/aggregate/route before ingest; Abstract reports 70–80% volume reduction (demo here: ~34:1 aggregation, ~99.6% routed off the SIEM).
capabilityGap.whyItMatters: The SIEM bill is a volume bill. Cutting volume at the source is the largest, most durable cost lever.

capabilityGap.sentinel: Ingests what you send; limited native dedup/aggregation.
capabilityGap.abstract: Aggregation, dedupe, filtering and down-sampling in-stream (aggregation_count on every record).
capabilityGap.whyItMatters: Most SIEM volume is repetitive/benign; collapsing it upstream is pure savings + less analyst noise.

capabilityGap.sentinel: Tiered: Analytics ~$4.30/GB, Basic $0.50/GB, Auxiliary $0.05/GB (+$0.10 processing), and the data lake (GA Oct 2025) ~$0.05/GB ingest + $0.026/GB-mo — but tiering + retention are managed inside the SIEM, per source.
capabilityGap.abstract: LakeVilla full-fidelity cold tier, always query-ready; replay with no rehydration, decided upstream and independent of any SIEM.
capabilityGap.whyItMatters: Keep everything affordably and still hunt it retroactively — and your tiering decision isn't locked to one SIEM's pricing.

capabilityGap.sentinel: ASIM, applied post-ingest with per-source parsers.
capabilityGap.abstract: OCSF + Abstract Common Schema (473 fields), normalized once in-stream before landing.
capabilityGap.whyItMatters: Normalize-once means the same detections/queries work across any vendor's data.

capabilityGap.sentinel: Scheduled analytics rules over already-ingested data.
capabilityGap.abstract: Six shift-left in-stream detections at ~0.5s (verdict fusion, IOC blast-match, beaconing, ATO↔C2, lateral/exfil, campaign clustering).
capabilityGap.whyItMatters: Detecting before ingest shortens time-to-detect and avoids paying to store what you were going to alert on anyway.

capabilityGap.abstract: 5-step in-stream enrichment (identity/asset, geo/ASN, TI/AIG, 29+ OSINT adapters, verdict fusion) — 100% coverage.
capabilityGap.whyItMatters: Enriched-at-landing data means higher-fidelity detections and less swivel-chair during triage.

capabilityGap.sentinel: UEBA add-on; entities scoped per incident.
capabilityGap.abstract: Cross-source identity/entity graph (10 entity types) with cumulative risk scoring across products.
capabilityGap.whyItMatters: Cross-product identity risk is a signal a per-incident SIEM view rarely assembles on its own.

capabilityGap.sentinel: Security Copilot — a prompt-based assistant (add-on) layered on the SIEM.
capabilityGap.abstract: ASTRO — an AI security engineer embedded in the platform — auto-triages, investigates and tunes detections over pipeline data + case context (Verdict, IP Threat Intelligence, and more).
capabilityGap.whyItMatters: Auto-triage + recommended actions reach the analyst with the case, not after they start digging.

capabilityGap.sentinel: Raw alerts → incidents; analysts triage the noise.
capabilityGap.abstract: Correlated, verdicted insights (finding + context); noise collapsed upstream.
capabilityGap.whyItMatters: Fewer, richer, decision-ready items lowers alert fatigue and mean-time-to-decision.

capabilityGap.sentinel: Tune rules post-ingest — you still pay to ingest the noise.
capabilityGap.whyItMatters: A false-positive disposition permanently lowers *future* ingest AND future incidents — not just this one.

capabilityGap.abstract: OCSF pipeline routes the same model to Sentinel, Splunk, any SIEM, Event Hub, LakeVilla.
capabilityGap.whyItMatters: Heterogeneous / M&A estates get one model; destinations become a per-cost choice.

capabilityGap.sentinel: Data + detections live in the SIEM; switching = re-onboarding sources and rewriting content.
capabilityGap.abstract: Pipeline decouples sources from the SIEM; portable normalization + detections; SIEM is a swappable destination.
capabilityGap.whyItMatters: Decoupling protects negotiating leverage and makes future platform changes low-risk.

capabilityGap.sentinel: Logic Apps playbooks bill per action; automation volume scales with incident/alert volume.
capabilityGap.abstract: Fewer, higher-fidelity insights + upstream tune-at-source mean fewer incidents to automate against.
capabilityGap.whyItMatters: Cutting incident volume upstream lowers both SIEM ingest AND downstream automation spend.

capabilityGap.sentinel: One workspace is the destination; multi-SIEM or migration means re-onboarding sources.
capabilityGap.abstract: Fan out the same normalized events + findings simultaneously — Abstract lists Sentinel, Splunk, AWS Security Lake, CrowdStrike NG-SIEM, Elastic, Google SecOps, Cortex XSIAM and SentinelOne as destinations.
capabilityGap.whyItMatters: Run a bake-off, support M&A/mixed estates, or migrate with no source re-onboarding.

capabilityGap.sentinel: Masking/redaction configured post-ingest or via connectors; sensitive data can land before it's handled.
capabilityGap.abstract: Abstract states PII is detected and redacted in-stream (GDPR/HIPAA/PCI) before data reaches any destination.
capabilityGap.whyItMatters: Sensitive fields never hit the SIEM in the clear — compliance handled upstream, not after landing.

capabilityGap.sentinel: Per-source connectors + ASIM parser upkeep as sources and schemas change.
capabilityGap.abstract: Normalize once to OCSF/ACS upstream; new sources map once and every downstream query still works.
capabilityGap.whyItMatters: Less parser/rule maintenance as the estate changes — engineering time back to the SOC.

capabilityGap.abstract: Bidirectional: feeds Sentinel (destination) AND reads back via API (verdict, search, tune-at-source).
capabilityGap.whyItMatters: Transparent two-way integration — augment today, rebalance later, on your timeline.

migrationLadder.detail: Keep Sentinel exactly as-is. Route Abstract findings + enriched context in via the destination connector; pull insights/verdicts back via the API connector. Immediate fidelity + AI-SOC uplift, zero disruption.
Send only convictions + supporting context to Sentinel; route full-fidelity telemetry to LakeVilla. Volume-based ingest drops sharply (demo: ~99.6%) while retention/hunt coverage stays complete.
With normalization + detections living in the pipeline, the SIEM becomes a swappable, per-cost destination. Evaluate augment-vs-replace on real numbers — using the TCO panels in this solution.

leanTogetherWhen: Microsoft-heavy estate — Defender XDR, Entra, M365 already correlate in Sentinel.
Compliance, reporting and IR runbooks are standardized in Sentinel today.
The team is fluent in KQL and Sentinel content and wants uplift, not change.
Goal is higher fidelity + AI-SOC (ASTRO) + cost relief with zero disruption.
You want a fast, reversible win to prove value before any bigger decision.
leanWithoutWhen: SIEM spend is the pain — a volume-driven bill growing faster than the security value.
Multi-SIEM / multi-cloud / vendor-neutral mandate; avoiding lock-in is strategic.
Retention-heavy (long compliance windows) — hot-tier-everything doesn't scale.
Noisy high-volume sources (firewall, DNS, proxy, flow) dominate ingestion.
Migrating off a legacy or over-priced SIEM — you want a durable pipeline layer first.

useCases.why: Route Abstract findings + context into Sentinel; add ASTRO verdicts and tune-at-source. Keep everything you have, raise fidelity, trim noise.
Send convictions + context to Sentinel, full fidelity to LakeVilla. Volume-based bill drops sharply (demo: ~99.6%) with no loss of hunt coverage.
Normalize once, fan out to Sentinel, Splunk, any SIEM simultaneously. Run a bake-off or consolidate without re-onboarding sources.
Keep multi-year full-fidelity in an always-queryable cold tier with replay; send only what the SIEM needs to the hot tier.
Stand up the pipeline first; detections + normalization live in Abstract, so the SIEM becomes a swappable, per-cost destination and migration is low-risk.
Feed agents decision-ready insights + an entity graph via API/MCP; Sentinel + Copilot and ASTRO operate on signal, not raw log soup.

positioningPOV.title: Speed vs. scale
positioningPOV.detail: Abstract is pipeline-native and focused — one hard problem, solved deeply, shipped fast. A hyperscaler bundles the SIEM into a vast platform and ships on platform time; a focused vendor iterates on pipeline economics and detections at startup speed.

positioningPOV.title: Incentive alignment
positioningPOV.detail: A per-GB SIEM earns more the more you ingest — the opposite of your cost goal. A pipeline earns by making your data smaller and smarter. Align spend with a vendor whose incentive is your reduction, not your volume.

positioningPOV.title: Neutral by design
positioningPOV.detail: Abstract is Switzerland for security data — it doesn't need you all-in on one cloud or SIEM. That neutrality is the hedge: detections, normalization and history stay portable however the platform market shifts.

positioningPOV.title: Focused roadmap
positioningPOV.detail: Pipeline, cost, fidelity and AI-SOC are the whole roadmap here — not line items competing with hundreds of other platform priorities. Requests land with the team that owns the problem end to end.

positioningPOV.title: Adopt the future without betting the SOC
positioningPOV.detail: Because it's additive and reversible, put Abstract in front of Sentinel today and decide augment-vs-replace later — moving as fast as your risk tolerance allows, not as fast as a migration forces.

futureProof.title: Own your data gravity
futureProof.detail: Normalizing to OCSF upstream means your detections, enrichment and history aren't trapped in one SIEM's schema. When the market shifts — new SIEM, new tier, new owner — your security logic travels with you instead of being rewritten.

futureProof.title: AI-ready by construction
futureProof.detail: Agentic SOC needs clean, correlated, enriched, entity-resolved data — not raw log soup. Abstract lands decision-ready insights + a queryable entity graph, and exposes them to agents via API/MCP, so ASTRO and your own AI stack operate on signal, not noise.

futureProof.title: Ride Microsoft's own roadmap without the lock-in
futureProof.detail: Microsoft's own Sentinel data lake (GA Oct 2025) and Basic/Auxiliary tiers price cheap storage at ~$0.05/GB vs. ~$4.30/GB for Analytics — proof of the pre-SIEM-curation thesis Abstract already delivers. Abstract lets you apply that economics upstream and across every SIEM you run, not just inside one.

futureProof.title: Retention economics that scale with regulation
futureProof.detail: As retention mandates grow, hot-tier-everything doesn't scale. Full-fidelity in an always-queryable cold tier (LakeVilla) with replay lets you satisfy multi-year retention and still hunt it — without multiplying SIEM ingest.

futureProof.title: One model across a consolidating estate
futureProof.detail: M&A, multi-cloud and tool consolidation are constant. A vendor- and destination-agnostic pipeline lets you absorb new sources and route to new destinations without re-onboarding or rewriting content each time.
